description: Protocol-agnostic mandate & guardrail layer for agentic commerce — Razorpay AI Buildathon Track 01

userStories.title: Project scaffold & repo init
userStories.description: Initialize the monorepo folder structure: backend/ (FastAPI), frontend/ (React/Vite), agent/ (test harness). Add requirements.txt, .env.example, .gitignore, and a root README skeleton.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/ has a runnable FastAPI app on port 8000 returning {status: ok} at GET /health
frontend/ has a Vite+React app scaffolded
agent/ folder exists with a placeholder script
.env.example documents all required env vars
.gitignore covers Python, Node, and .env

userStories.title: Merchant UCP manifest endpoint
userStories.description: Serve a UCP-style agent-discoverable catalog at GET /.well-known/ucp. The manifest lists available product categories, merchant metadata, and TrustRail capability flags (mandate_required: true).
acceptanceCriteria: GET /.well-known/ucp returns valid JSON with merchant name, allowed categories, and mandate_required: true
Categories include at least: groceries, household, electronics
Endpoint is CORS-enabled for agent access

userStories.title: Mandate schema + database setup
userStories.description: Define the SQLite DB schema for mandates and audit_log tables. Mandate schema matches Section 6.2 of the PRD (mandate_id, issuer_user_id, agent_id, merchant_id, scope JSON, issued_at, expires_at, revoked, signature, protocol_origin). Use SQLAlchemy ORM.
acceptanceCriteria: Running `python -m backend.db.init` creates the DB and both tables
Mandate model has all fields from PRD Section 6.2
audit_log table has: id, mandate_id, event_type, decision, rules_checked JSON, reason, created_at, prev_hash (for hash-chaining)

userStories.title: Mandate issuance API
userStories.description: POST /mandates creates a new mandate. Generates a mandate_id (mnd_ prefix + UUID), signs the mandate payload with Ed25519 (server keypair stored in .env), saves to DB, returns the signed mandate JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /mandates with valid body returns 201 with mandate JSON including signature field
Signature is valid Ed25519 over the mandate payload (excluding signature field)
mandate_id starts with mnd_
Mandate is persisted to DB

userStories.title: Mandate revocation API
userStories.description: DELETE /mandates/:mandate_id sets revoked=true on the mandate. Returns 200 on success, 404 if not found.
acceptanceCriteria: DELETE /mandates/:id sets revoked=true in DB
Subsequent guardrail checks on a revoked mandate return BLOCK with reason revoked
Returns 404 for unknown mandate_id

userStories.title: Guardrail engine — signature, expiry, category rules
userStories.description: Build the core guardrail module (backend/guardrail/engine.py) as a pure Python module with no DB/API dependencies. Implement rules 1–3 from PRD Section 6.3: signature validation, expiry/revocation check, category scope check. Each rule returns a RuleResult(passed: bool, rule: str, reason: str).
acceptanceCriteria: engine.validate_mandate(mandate, request) returns a GuardrailDecision(allowed: bool, rules: list[RuleResult])
Rule 1: invalid signature → BLOCK invalid_signature
Rule 2: expired mandate → BLOCK expired; revoked → BLOCK revoked
Rule 3: category not in allowed_categories → BLOCK out_of_scope_category
All rules evaluated even if one fails (no short-circuit)
Unit tests for all 3 rules passing and failing cases

userStories.title: Guardrail engine — spend cap and replay rules
userStories.description: Add rules 4–7 to the guardrail engine: per-transaction cap, rolling 7-day cap (requires DB lookup for spend sum), replay detection (nonce uniqueness), and the ALLOW path that returns a signed execution token.
acceptanceCriteria: Rule 4: amount > max_per_transaction → BLOCK exceeds_transaction_cap
Rule 5: trailing 7d spend + requested amount > max_rolling_7d → BLOCK exceeds_rolling_cap
Rule 6: nonce already seen for this mandate → BLOCK replay_detected
Rule 7: all pass → ALLOW, returns signed execution_token
Unit tests for all 4 rules

userStories.title: Hash-chained audit log writer
userStories.description: Every guardrail decision (ALLOW or BLOCK) is appended to the audit_log table. Each row includes a SHA-256 hash of the previous row's hash + current row data (hash chaining for tamper-evidence). Expose GET /audit-log endpoint returning the full log.
acceptanceCriteria: Every call to the guardrail engine appends a row to audit_log
Each row's hash = SHA256(prev_hash + mandate_id + decision + timestamp)
First row uses hash of empty string as prev_hash
GET /audit-log returns all rows in order with all fields

userStories.title: Razorpay happy path integration
userStories.description: POST /pay endpoint: accepts a payment request (mandate_id, amount, category, nonce), runs guardrail engine, if ALLOW calls Razorpay test-mode Orders API to create an order, logs to audit trail, returns order details. If BLOCK, returns structured refusal.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /pay with valid mandate returns 200 with Razorpay order_id
POST /pay with invalid mandate returns 402 with block reason and full rules checklist
Razorpay API key loaded from RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET env vars
Every /pay call — allowed or blocked — is logged to audit_log

userStories.title: UCP protocol adapter
userStories.description: Build backend/adapters/ucp.py: maps an incoming UCP-style checkout call (with catalog item reference and buyer agent ID) into the internal Mandate Request format. Wire it to a POST /adapters/ucp/checkout endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /adapters/ucp/checkout accepts UCP-shaped payload and normalizes to internal MandateRequest
Normalized request flows through guardrail engine and returns UCP-compatible response
Adapter is isolated — only converts shapes, no business logic

userStories.title: AP2 protocol adapter
userStories.description: Build backend/adapters/ap2.py: accepts AP2-style signed mandate/intent objects, verifies the AP2 signature scheme, maps fields into the internal mandate schema. Wire to POST /adapters/ap2/intent.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /adapters/ap2/intent accepts AP2-shaped payload
Signature verification step is present (even if using our own Ed25519 as a stand-in for AP2's VC scheme)
Maps to internal MandateRequest and flows through guardrail
Protocol_origin field set to ap2 in mandate

userStories.title: UAP-ready stub adapter + mapping doc
userStories.description: Build backend/adapters/uap_ready.py as a documented stub. Write docs/uap-mapping.md: a table mapping UAP reported concepts (delegation, spend limits, agent registry, human-reviewable logs) to TrustRail internal fields. Be explicit about what is confirmed vs anticipated.
acceptanceCriteria: backend/adapters/uap_ready.py exists with clearly documented TODO markers and field mapping comments
docs/uap-mapping.md contains the protocol comparison table for all 3 protocols (UCP, AP2, UAP)
Document explicitly labels each UAP field as confirmed or anticipated

userStories.title: AI buyer agent test harness — happy path + adversarial scenarios
userStories.description: Build agent/harness.py: a scripted agent that runs all 7 adversarial scenarios from PRD Section 10 against the live backend. Each scenario prints PASS/FAIL with the actual vs expected guardrail decision.
acceptanceCriteria: All 7 scenarios from PRD Section 10 are implemented
Scenario 1 (happy path) → ALLOW
Scenarios 2–6 → BLOCK with correct violation reason
Scenario 7 (prompt injection in catalog) → BLOCK (rule-based, not LLM-persuadable)
Script outputs a summary table: scenario, expected, actual, pass/fail

userStories.title: Reviewer dashboard — audit trail + metrics
userStories.description: Build the React frontend dashboard: a timeline view of all audit log entries (mandate_id, decision, reason, timestamp), a block-rate metric card (% blocked vs allowed), and a Revoke Mandate button that calls DELETE /mandates/:id.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard fetches and displays GET /audit-log entries in a timeline
Block rate metric (blocked / total) shown as a percentage card
Each audit entry shows: mandate_id, decision (ALLOW/BLOCK badge), reason, timestamp
Revoke button calls DELETE /mandates/:id and refreshes the log
Verify in browser that all 3 elements render correctly

userStories.title: Metrics batch run + README
userStories.description: Run the full test batch: ≥20 happy-path runs + all 7 adversarial cases. Capture metrics from PRD Section 9. Write the final README with architecture diagram, protocol comparison table link, how-to-run instructions, and honest limitations section.
acceptanceCriteria: 100% of executed test-mode payments traceable to a valid mandate
≥4 adversarial scenarios blocked with correct violation reason
Guardrail validation latency measured and documented (target <300ms)
Zero false-blocks on the 20-run happy path batch
README has: architecture overview, how to run, protocol table link, limitations
